scenarios.title: Visitor sees the public sign-in form
preconditions: The public login page is available.
given: The public login page is available.
when: A visitor opens the sign-in page.
then: The page title is "Sign in — ZincTM".
The sign-in form presents Email and Password fields.
The sign-in form offers a "Sign in" action.
The Email and Password fields are empty on initial load.
expectedResults: The rendered title is "Sign in — ZincTM".
The ZincALM heading, Email and Password fields, and Sign in action are present on the initial page.
Both credential fields are empty on initial load.

evidence.detail: The title, heading, Email and Password fields, and Sign in button were observed; both fields were empty on initial load.
The accessibility snapshot records the visible heading, empty textboxes, and Sign in button.
The public page loaded at the supplied URL; the workflow stopped before any form interaction.

openQuestions: Which approved product requirement or acceptance criterion should this observed-page characterization trace to?

scenarios.title: Sign-in form identifies both credentials as required
preconditions: The public login page is available.
given: A visitor is on the public login page.
when: The visitor views the initial sign-in form.
then: The Email field is required and uses email input semantics.
The Password field is required and uses password input semantics.
expectedResults: The Email input is configured as required with email input semantics.
The Password input is configured as required with password input semantics.

evidence.detail: The Email input is type=email and required; the Password input is type=password and required. No form submission or validation response was tested.
Both credential inputs and their required states and input types are documented from page inspection.

openQuestions: Which approved product requirement or acceptance criterion confirms the intended required credential fields?
What should happen after submitting valid credentials?
What should happen after empty or malformed credentials are submitted? No validation or submission behavior was observed, so no outcomes are asserted here.
Does the empty alert node in the accessibility snapshot represent any intended user-visible feedback?

coverageGaps: No product requirements, user stories, or acceptance criteria were found in the supplied project materials; requirement traceability is pending clarification.

Successful and unsuccessful submission, empty-field submission, email-format validation, alert content, and post-authentication navigation were not explored and are excluded rather than assigned expected results.

The form's observed method is GET with action /login. This markup observation does not establish intended credential handling; do not add a submission scenario until expected behavior and an approved synthetic test setup are confirmed.
An empty alert node appears in the accessibility snapshot, but its source and purpose are unknown; no alert behavior is asserted.
